operations.comment: ; Pitch/field marker search view of scene-shared CPU RAM.
; Scoped field-upload/preview scratch and IRQ aliases; these CPU RAM locations are reused by other scenes.
; Sound-test overlay and scene-local iteration bounds.
; Shop preview overlay: six equipment bytes begin at D1; high-bit entries use alternate visuals.
; Ending-intro overlay; later ending segments reuse other scene variables.
; Duel scene overlay: paired actor arrays use index zero/one; these addresses have different roles in pitch and menu scenes.
; Scene-local overlays; values are reused by other screen modes.
; Gameplay world/trajectory fields (bank-pair four) and pitch-local fields (pair six).
; Array indices distinguish actor slots from two-byte coordinate offsets.
; Shared state and NES hardware. CPU aliases are not physical ROM identities.
; Dedicated audio state; six logical slots share channel-array bases.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $000000..$000010.
; iNES header: mapper, PRG and CHR sizes; preserve the original sixteen bytes.

; Physical $000010..$000011: Logical PRG pair identity 0, read at CPU $8000 by the mapper save helper. Restore supports saved tags zero through six; this byte is Data, separate from the following entry instruction.

; Advance the six logical sound streams. X is the channel index, saved across APU writes. Pause suppresses ordinary streams but leaves sound $23 active. Physical $10 is the logical pair-zero identity byte; this is the first Code instruction.
; Clear stream state and the shared pause latch on this resume path, then join ordinary stream selection.
; When pause state changes, restore pulse 1 unless the overriding stream $23 owns it.
; Remember pause state. Fade progression and tempo stretching run only while unpaused.
; Every $25 ticks advance the fade stage; stages four and five stop selected streams, and stage six clears the engine.
; Periodically extend the remaining note counters of channels 0, 1, 2 and 5 by one tick.
; Visit six logical slots; only slots with a nonzero sound ID are serviced.
; Load this stream pointer and test whether pause permits an update. Channel 2 has triangle-specific linear-counter decay.
; A zero note countdown resumes command parsing. Other ticks update envelopes and pitch effects.
; At sixteen-tick intervals reduce the triangle linear-counter value by $40 without underflow. The delay helper preserves spacing between APU writes.
; Rewrite the triangle high timer with bit three set, then refresh stream state through the common helper.
; Slots 4 and 5 skip sustained pitch/envelope work. Slot 2 takes the triangle path; other slots honor rest and direct-note flags.
; For enabled pulse pitch stepping, repeatedly subtract the tick unit to find the note phase. Update the phase index at exact multiples.

; Preserve stream cursor Y. Choose one of four phase-period slots, with the second hardware voice using slots four through seven, then capture the current two-byte period. Duration decides whether to resume ordinary pitch processing.
; Select one of four cached periods, with a second four-entry group for pulse 2. Preserve the stream cursor while committing the period.
; Flag $02 enables timed modulation steps. Reload the modulation delay and recompute the pitch when its countdown expires.
; Advance the volume-envelope position when its delay expires.
; Compare remaining duration with the derived release threshold; the envelope flags choose forward progression or reverse decay.
; Combine channel control bits with an envelope or explicit control override. Below the release threshold, the secondary decay counter attenuates the output.

; Read the next stream byte through the audio cursor. Bytes $FB..$FF select control handlers; lower values select ordinary/direct notes according to stream flag one. The return-consuming dispatch tables are stored separately as Data.

; Physical $00024C..$000256: 5 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Commit the command cursor, remember it as this channel's loop start, then reload the active cursor.

; Advance Y and resume the audio stream parser with the existing channel, cursor and stream state. This tail entry shares the surrounding command handlers' contract; natural command selection is unresolved.
; Set the subsequence-active flag, load the target stream and save the post-operand cursor for the return command. Rejoin the parser without advancing its new target.
; An $FF count repeats indefinitely; zero ends the loop. Other counts compare the incremented loop counter, restoring the saved stream pointer until the requested count is met.
; Clear the loop count and consume the repeat command before parsing its successor.

; Flag $20 selects the saved subsequence-continuation path. Otherwise disable the slot and clear its software flags; silence hardware unless another stream owns it. Stream-level cycles do not establish universal tick termination.
; Restore the saved per-slot stream cursor and continue parsing there. This is the stream-level return path; cyclic command streams need not terminate in one tick.
; Finishing slot 3 restores pulse 1 if slot 0 is active. Triangle shutdown writes a zero control value and $FF timer-high shadow.
; Bytes below $D0 are notes; higher bytes use their high nibble to select a command handler through the inline-table dispatcher.

; Physical $000328..$00032E: 3 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Set the low-nibble tick multiplier. Slot 5 returns directly to parsing; other channels read the packed volume/control byte, then envelope and release parameters.
; Separate the control high nibble from the low-nibble initial attenuation. Triangle uses the full parameter byte instead.
; Clear this slot's attenuation before initializing the new note.
; Store packed release parameters. A zero high nibble is normalized to one before initializing the envelope delay.
; Low nibbles below six select an octave; higher values enter channel-specific extended-parameter dispatch. Several handlers are not yet structurally classified.

; Physical $00039D..$0003B1: 10 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.

; Physical $0003B4..$0003C8: 10 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Skip two command bytes and join the shared parameter reader.
; Consume another parameter while the next high nibble is $E0; otherwise resume normal stream decoding.
; Store the octave/period-shift selector for this logical channel.
; Update the low-nibble attenuation without changing other channel parameters.
; Read a full-byte note-duration multiplier, then resume parsing.
; Read the next stream byte as the envelope selector and resume command decoding.
; Read a full-byte packed release parameter.
; Nonzero low bits enable explicit control overrides; zero clears them. The connected override paths are classified separately below.
; Copy the command parameter to the slot's APU control shadow.
; Clear the override and consume its byte.
; Read the signed-nibble transpose encoding consumed by audio_decode_transpose.
; Zero disables modulation. Otherwise subtract $50 to obtain the modulation-table selector, set flag $02 and read packed timing/depth.
; Multiply the tick unit by the packed high-nibble factor; zero keeps the existing accumulator path. The low nibble supplies a nonzero depth multiplier.
; Clear stream flag $02 and continue parsing.
; Read a phase mode from the stream. Zero disables modulation; nonzero modes normalize values above three into the alternate mode flag and restart the phase index.
; Store the encoded period adjustment. High bit means addition of the low seven bits; a positive byte is subtracted later.
; Set the global stretch period and restart its tick counter.
; Slot five interprets note high nibbles as event requests. Values below five start stream descriptors; higher values select DMC requests through the remap backing.
; Physical $0004E6..$0004F2: Audio requested sound remap backing. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; Commit the stream cursor. The note low nibble scales the tick unit, with zero meaning sixteen; slot 5 delegates to event playback.
; High nibble $C0 marks a rest and silences the channel while retaining its other parameters.
; Clear the rest flag, then initialize triangle linear timing or the pulse/noise release and envelope state.
; Combine encoded triangle timing with note duration, saturating to the engine's $81 fallback on overflow or zero.
; Compute floor(note_ticks * low_release_nibble / 16) using a sixteen-bit intermediate.
; Reset envelope/modulation indices and counters for the new note. Choose an initial envelope state according to its direction flag.
; Build the initial control/volume register with any explicit override; suppress pulse 1 writes while the overriding slot owns it.
; Add signed transpose to the note high nibble and bias by twelve. Read the little-endian period table, shift it until the selected octave reaches five, and set timer-high bit $08.

; Pulse slots maintain a four-phase period cache. Disabled/high-bit state skips capture; initialization seeds all four entries, while ordinary updates replace the phase-selected entry and preserve stream cursor Y.
; Seed four period-history entries for this voice from its current period while preserving the stream cursor. Voice one uses the second four-entry group.
; Seed the next two-byte period-history slot; three decrements after initial count three visit four entries.
; Replace the period-history entry selected by phase low bits, preserving stream cursor Y for the shared continuation.
; Load the base period. Triangle bypasses pulse adjustments; other slots apply modulation and encoded period offset before writing timer registers.
; Add signed eight-bit modulation to the sixteen-bit period with carry or borrow into its high byte.
; Apply the channel's encoded fixed adjustment: high-bit values add their magnitude, other nonzero values subtract it.
; Avoid redundant timer-high writes, except when control flags require retriggering. Always update the timer-low shadow and hardware when ownership permits.
; Physical $00073D..$000785: Audio note-period words. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; If bit seven is set, negate the low nibble; otherwise return the raw transpose byte. This encoding is distinct from a conventional signed byte.
; Resolve the selected modulation script, decode a delay in the high nibble and a signed four-bit delta in the low nibble, and scale the delta by channel depth.
; Multiply the low-nibble delta by the nonzero modulation depth through repeated addition.
; Copy the channel's base period into the shared sixteen-bit work pair.
; Resolve the envelope script and decode its high nibble as delay and low nibble as volume. Preserve the caller's stream cursor.
; Subtract initial attenuation, release attenuation and global fade stage from envelope volume; clamp at one and combine with control bits.
; During release, override control bits only when the explicit-release flag is enabled.
; Load the channel's stored APU control high bits into the shared work byte.
; Read envelope bytes below $FB as values. Higher bytes save/reload loop positions, count repeats or hold the last value; connected handlers preserve those restart and repeat slots.
; Save the current envelope position into its restart slot, then continue parsing envelope controls.
; Restore the saved envelope position and reenter the envelope parser.
; Advance the envelope position before returning to its parser.
; Read modulation values below $FB. Control bytes maintain a saved loop index and repetition count; $FF holds the previous position.
; Advance modulation position and resume its control parser.
; Resume modulation parsing after the preceding repeat-state update.
; Eight NOPs provide fixed spacing between register writes. No logical channel state changes.
; Load channel stream pointer into the shared zero-page cursor and reset Y to zero.
; Advance the saved channel pointer past Y, carrying into its high byte. The working cursor itself is reloaded by callers when needed.
; Read a little-endian stream target following the command. Y advances across both pointer bytes; the source cursor itself is unchanged.
; Save cursor plus Y plus one as this slot's continuation after the two-byte target. The parser later restores it on the stream return command.
; Map a logical channel to its APU register group and write control register zero.
; Map a logical channel and write register one (pulse sweep where applicable).
; Map a logical channel and write timer-low register two.
; Map a logical channel and write timer-high register three.
; Translate logical slot through the six-byte register-offset table, preserving the value in A. Callers restore X after the write delay.

; Physical $00094C..$000952: Audio channel to hardware register group. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; Delay after the hardware write and restore the current logical slot.
; Return carry set only when slot 0 is masked by active slot 3. Preserve the register value in A.
; Silence pulse/noise control registers and triangle linear counter; update the triangle high-byte shadow. DMC is handled separately.
; Restore pulse 1 sweep and cached timer after an overriding stream finishes. Rebuild volume only for an active, unpaused, non-rest stream.

; A is an index into little-endian addresses immediately after the JSR. Pop the return address, select the indexed target, restore X/Y and jump indirectly; execution does not return through the inline table.
; Direct streams interpret zero high nibbles as channel-parameter updates; nonzero high nibbles encode hardware note data.
; A zero byte reuses the tick unit and silences pulse 1. Otherwise store duration, control high bits and sweep byte; values zero/$88 clear the retrigger flag.
; Store the duration parameter, then read the triangle linear-counter byte and refresh stream state through the connected continuation.
; Read the next stream byte directly into the triangle linear-counter register, refresh stream state, and resume command parsing.
; A zero byte reuses duration and silences noise; otherwise set duration and the noise control high bits.
; Route triangle/noise separately. Pulse bytes $E6..$EF dispatch special commands; other values provide control and a packed timer.
; Unless stream flag $20 retains the current period, read three high period bits and one low byte. Then use the common period writer and commit the cursor.
; Reuse the configured note duration and follow the connected duration-selection branch into the shared stream continuation.
; Noise consumes a low-nibble period, with $10 taking an additional byte. Reuse common control-volume construction.
; Reload duration and derive volume from the high nibble. Apply fade/attenuation with a floor of one, then combine with stored control bits.
; Bytes $E6 and above select the inline command-handler table. Each handler implements its parameter/state update before returning to parsing; cyclic streams need not finish within one tick.

; Physical $000B25..$000B39: 10 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Read this slot's duration unit from the stream and resume decoding.
; Toggle stream flag bit five and resume decoding; this flag participates in the stream-level call/return mechanism.
; Keep the low parameter nibble as slot attenuation.
; Keep the high parameter nibble as the slot's control bits.
; One $FF byte between the completed audio-control jump and reset entry. The instruction interpretation would borrow reset bytes; retain generic data without claiming a terminator or fill purpose.
; Clear six slot IDs, flags and timer-high shadows plus shared fade/tempo/DMC cooldown state; preserve X and tail-call APU silence.
; A supplies a sound/event ID. Reject selected requests under game-state gates, treat $3D as fade, values $3E+ as reset, and route $31..$3C to DMC.

; Look up a stream descriptor. Its top two bits encode additional channel records, low three bits select a logical slot, and bit $20 chooses direct format. Lower-priority IDs do not replace higher IDs already active.
; Clear channel effects and loop count according to channel type; prime duration to one and copy the descriptor's stream pointer into current and loop-start fields.
; Initialize APU sweep/control/timer defaults when this slot owns the hardware; pulse 1 may be masked by slot 3.
; Record the requested sound ID and consume further three-byte channel records while the descriptor count remains.

; Reject samples during the cooldown. Index the cooldown table with ID-$31, select a four-byte record at fixed CPU $F800, disable DMC, write $4013..$4010 in reverse order and enable it again. This fixed-bank sample setup does not identify the sample payload extent.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $000CD5..$002010.

; Audio descriptors and command/note stream backing. Consumers use three-byte channel descriptors and finite stream controls; repeated note/duration patterns support non-code storage. The entire musical grammar and sound names remain unresolved.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $002010..$003703.

; Audio descriptors and command/note stream backing. Consumers use three-byte channel descriptors and finite stream controls; repeated note/duration patterns support non-code storage. The entire musical grammar and sound names remain unresolved.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $003703..$004010.
; Uniform byte run with exact reviewed boundaries. No accepted code conflicts; original fill or backing-data purpose remains unresolved.

; Physical $004010..$004011: Logical PRG pair identity 1, read at CPU $8000 by the mapper save helper. Restore supports saved tags zero through six; this byte is Data, separate from the following entry instruction.
; Check the controller skip contract before entering the inline ending state dispatcher.
; Run the shared ending update before dispatching the current phase. The outer table requires the established phase range; this entry does not clamp it.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $00401C..$00403A.
; Fifteen inline little-endian state destinations. The independent helper at CPU $802A bounds the table; pointer-looking bytes beyond it are executable helper bytes, not additional entries.
; Return normally unless controller bit seven is set. On skip, discard this helper caller return address and jump directly to ending cleanup; the stack unwind is intentional.
; Clear local phase counters, initialize display/queue state and palette shadows, select the ending display mode and load resource $38. The ending dispatcher owns subsequent phase progression.
; Load the paired background resources, reset display state, select audio and configure the split IRQ. Seed the extra sprite and advance the ending phase.

; Use primary pressed buttons to cycle the image and row, and held directional values to move sprite zero by one pixel. Redraw the two related ending images using the selected row. Image wraps at 27 and row at four; the scene owns these overlay fields.
; Advance the image; reaching 27 advances the four-row selector and clears the image index.
; Wrap the row to zero after the fourth row.
; Move sprite zero right one pixel.
; Move sprite zero left one pixel.
; Move sprite zero down one pixel.
; Move sprite zero up one pixel.
; Dispatch the current local phase through the following inline table.

; Physical $004119..$00411D: 2 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Place four initial images for this ending segment, then advance its local state.
; Move the first image down to row $40 and the second on alternate ticks. Once the second reaches the row, advance the phase and reset local counters.
; Dispatch the next ending sequence using the local phase byte.

; Physical $004184..$00418E: 5 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.

; Unclassified physical $00418E..$00418F. Single RTS omitted by the neighboring dispatch table. An empty routine with an ordinary caller stack and a return-valued data residue remain materially indistinguishable.
; Hold this local state for sixteen ticks before advancing.
; Select the paired resting images and hold them for five ticks.
; Use adjacent eight-entry image rows, indexed by half-rate low timer bits. Selected timer positions raise the shared request flag; the $FF terminal tick restores resting images.
; Request resource nine through the common banked resource entry.
; Raise the shared scene request and continue the timer path.
; Reset both local counters before entering the next ending phase.

; Physical $00420B..$00421B: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Display images $3B/$3C and tick both sprite timers. Once the second timer expires, clear local counters and advance the outer sequence.
; Use the local phase to enter the next inline animation table.

; Physical $004244..$00424C: 4 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Place two images at the same X origin and reset their Y positions.
; Move both images on alternate ticks; at row $38 load another resource and hide the third image. Stop this descent at row $3F.
; Use timer bit two to select the paired images, then advance after four ticks.

; Physical $0042C4..$0042C8: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Move the second image upward until its Y wraps to zero; then hide it and advance.
; Increment the animation counter and use bits two through four to select a nonzero resource request. The zero phase produces no update.
; Check the local hold counter before completing this ending segment.

; Physical $0042F5..$0042FB: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Select the next audio request and extra image, then reset local counters and advance.
; Queue the same time-indexed color at palette offsets $1B and $1D. After 31 ticks, clear local state and advance the outer sequence.
; Append a single PPU palette write at $3F00 plus the selected palette offset. Counter bits one through four choose the color; append terminator and update queue cursor.
; Physical $00435D..$00436D: Palette animation values used by masked/shifted phase selection. Repeated mirrored color ramps and independent neighboring code bound the storage.
; Choose an image from eight entries using the counter divided by two. At counter $0E, reset local counters and advance the outer sequence.
; Physical $00438B..$004393: Ending foreground image cycle. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; Request resource $3D through the shared loader.
; Keep the fourth image at a fixed origin. Timer bits choose either image/resource pairs or resource-only pairs; the terminal count switches audio and advances.
; Physical $0043D0..$0043D8: Paired ending object images. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; Use timer bits three/four to choose the alternate resource row, then return to the shared completion test.
; Physical $0043EA..$0043F2: Ending object image sequence. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.

; Set the base image and emit selectors $11/$12/$13 and $01/$02/$03 through the existing ending-image helper. On alternate ticks advance the frame; frame 31 clears the two frame fields and advances the scene phase.
; Request resource $47 for the later ending sequence.
; Load the phase resource and enter the next phase with local counters cleared.

; On alternating ticks, queue colors for eight palette positions. Odd ticks request resource $6B; counter three triggers a transition resource and counter 31 advances to the next sequence with image $55.
; Emit the odd-tick resource update; the common counter/phase logic follows.
; Rejoin the earlier phase update after the selected branch-specific work.
; Rejoin the earlier phase tail; this path shares its state transition.
; Set image $55, clear local phase/counter and advance the ending sequence.
; Load the next ending display resource through the alternate resource entry.
; Clear both local counters and advance the ending phase.
; Load resource $57 through the alternate resource entry.
; Clear both local counters and advance the ending phase.
; Request the next ending resource through the common display entry.
; Clear both local counters and advance the ending phase.
; Count 128 ticks before transferring to the shared cleanup entry.
; Enter common cleanup; this is also the controller-skip destination.

; Physical $0044EC..$0044EF: Three-byte inline banked-call record: logical pair selector followed by little-endian CPU destination. The helper consumes the record from the stacked return address and resumes after it; effective physical bank context remains distinct from the selector byte.
; Return without changing the ending state.
; Queue one palette write at $3F0F, cycling an eight-color lookup with the counter divided by eight. Preserve all queue framing bytes and advance the cursor.
; Physical $004523..$00452B: Palette animation values used by masked/shifted phase selection. Repeated mirrored color ramps and independent neighboring code bound the storage.
; Dispatch outer sequence state through the following inline table.

; Physical $004530..$00453C: 6 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Load the scene resources and initialize the main image with fixed-point X/Y origins. Reset motion parameters, local states and palette animation before checking dismissal.
; Reset display, configure CHR/background and place 26 images from coordinate pairs. Initialize scroll, split IRQ and both motion state machines before advancing.

; Physical $00461B..$00464F: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Restore the main image origin and advance before checking dismissal.
; Use three image/duration records; advance the record only when its duration is exceeded, then advance the scene phase.

; Physical $004686..$00468C: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Advance the main image motion, optional companion images and palette cycle, then check dismissal.
; For animation kind three, mirror the main image into two offset companions during the first three local states; hide them in later states.
; Queue one palette byte at PPU $3F02. A six-bit tick advances through eight colors, holding each for eight updates.
; Physical $004708..$004710: Palette animation values used by masked/shifted phase selection. Repeated mirrored color ramps and independent neighboring code bound the storage.
; Advance scrolling and palette animation, update visibility and derive image X positions before checking dismissal.

; OR both newly pressed controller bytes and test bit seven. Accepted dismissal resets display and selects gameplay state five or eight according to the scene selector; the button name depends on the game's serialized bit order.
; For images one through 26, subtract the scroll-origin byte from stored X coordinates. Even slots double the result while odd slots keep the original difference.
; Walk images 26 through one. Compare their coordinates against row-dependent scroll thresholds and hide or restore the image as it crosses the visible window.
; Offset the inverted-scroll threshold by $18 above row $54 or $50 below it, subject to the byte limits checked here.
; Hide this image, then retain the shared right-edge check.
; Restore image $0D and continue the backward slot scan.
; Increment scroll toward $BF, then apply the vertical fixed-point parameter twice per update while reducing it to zero. Completion advances the outer phase.
; Unclassified physical $0047F0..$0047F1. Single RTS immediately after another RTS. The branch enters the following handler; empty routine versus return-valued residue remains unresolved.
; Quantize the main X coordinate into bands from $60 through $C0. The band number selects a resource; positions below the first band leave the display unchanged.
; Add the band index to resource $24 and enter the shared resource loader.
; Run horizontal and vertical motion dispatchers, then advance image IDs using the twelve-entry duration row.

; Physical $00485C..$00486A: Bounded lookup backing. 12 bounded row thresholds from 8833 CPY 0 C plus two same-pattern noncode tail bytes before 885 A Code; tail purpose unknown. Original declarations and natural selector completeness remain unproved.
; Dispatch the horizontal local state through its inline handler table.

; Physical $00486F..$00487B: 6 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Integrate horizontal position six times, increase the speed up to $80, and advance when X drops below $4A.
; Integrate position, reduce the horizontal parameter by three, and advance when the parameter becomes negative.
; Integrate rightward six times, increase speed by four up to $90 and update the resource band. At X $EA hide the image and advance both motion states.
; Load the final resource/audio pair and initialize the timed image sequence.
; Every third tick, advance image IDs $10..$16 and copy their coordinate pairs. When exhausted, hide the image and start the final delay.
; Count the delay until byte wrap, then enter the accepted dismissal transition.

; Physical $00492A..$004938: Finite indexed lookup backing. The nearby arithmetic/display consumer and complete local byte pattern were inspected against independent code boundaries. Exact original sublayout and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; Hide the main image and advance both motion-state counters.
; Subtract the horizontal parameter from the fixed-point X pair six times.
; Dispatch the vertical local state through its inline handler table.

; Physical $004954..$00495E: 5 little-endian inline handler destinations. The return-consuming dispatcher skips these words as instructions and selects a handler using its supported state contract; no arbitrary byte selector domain is implied.
; Integrate downward six times and increase speed to $80. Advance when Y reaches $9C.
; Integrate downward and reduce the vertical parameter by four until it becomes negative, then clear it and advance.
; Integrate upward and increase the vertical parameter by two until it reaches $4F.
; Integrate upward while reducing the vertical parameter by two; clamp at zero.
; Terminal vertical motion state returns without a change.
; Add the vertical parameter to the fixed-point Y pair six times.
; Subtract the vertical parameter from the fixed-point Y pair six times.
; Clear the scene counter and dispatch initialization by local state $80. The inline table is classified pointer data; the connected ending phase handlers preserve the established scene overlay.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $0049E4..$0049E8.
; Inline little-endian dispatch destinations. The shared dispatcher removes the JSR return address and indexes this table by state; these words are skipped as instruction bytes.

; Prepare display resources through fixed-bank helpers, initialize sprite slots and advance scene state. The artificial ending route displayed city/congratulations imagery with incomplete graphics; clean entry dependencies remain unresolved.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $004A17..$004A1A.
; Three-byte inline banked-call metadata: bank selector followed by little-endian CPU destination. The helper consumes it from the stacked return address and resumes after these three bytes.
; Set up transfer/display parameters and seed the first sprite record. Sprite properties are stored in parallel arrays at $0300 (image), $0320 (Y) and $0340 (X), not contiguous OAM records.
; Initialize six objects with alternating direction flags and table-derived Y positions, then initialize three transition counters and invoke the movement setup.
; Place the foreground animation sprites; derive slot 1 image from frame-counter bits 3..4.
; Update foreground animation and periodic moving objects, then dispatch the local animation phase in $81 through the classified handler table.
; Preserved reviewed subrange physical $004A94..$004B04.
; Inline little-endian dispatch destinations. The shared dispatcher removes the JSR return address and indexes this table by state; these words are skipped as instruction bytes.
; Select transition counter zero; the next two entries select counters one and two before joining shared logic.
; Active counters increment and toggle a phase flag on wrap. Early phases move sprite 2 upward; later phases derive its vertical position from the counter and select an animated image.
; Zero image hides the transition sprite. Other paths continue through the shared image assignment.
; For nonzero object indices move sprite 2 upward by two pixels until its coordinate becomes negative.
; When the shared delay expires, start the next object timer (for indices below two) and advance the local phase.

; Physical $004B70..$004B75: Ending foreground animation base images. Indexed consumers and exact neighboring code/metadata establish the stored extent; a complete natural selector domain is not implied.
; Advance three synchronized transition counters. When the first wraps, toggle all three parity bytes and advance ending phase.
; Start a 128-tick hold and advance ending phase.
; Continue the established motion helper during the hold; advance phase when the delay expires.
; Advance the secondary phase and request resource $61 followed by the resource indexed from $62. This extends the previously reviewed ending display path.
; Advance the secondary ending phase and return.
; Seed counter zero to $30 and advance the phase.
